Your flags are real. So is what labs miss.

Your lab flagged one food, all at low levels. That's a real finding, and it joins your elimination either way. But low-level flags alone rarely explain real symptoms, so the lab is the start of the answer, not the whole of it.

Some of the most common triggers, especially digestive ones like FODMAPs, don't show up on a lab panel at all. The most reliable next step is to test the usual suspects directly, alongside your flagged food, through the same structured elimination and reintroduction the protocol is built on.

You choose how thorough to go. And if you'd rather not run the full protocol right now, you can simply track your meals and symptoms instead, and start anytime.
